choice: Left means left of the direction of travel from start to end (north for an eastbound trip). Candidates are tried in the order 500 m left, 500 m right, 1000 m left, 1000 m right, 2000 m left, 2000 m right, 4000 m left, 4000 m right. The waypoint is measured in meters on the perpendicular through the start-end midpoint, with a tolerance of 2% of the offset plus 5 m. distanceM must be within 1% of the haversine length of the points.
options: All left offsets first (500, 1000, 2000, 4000), then all right offsets
Left means the positive perpendicular in raw lat/lon degrees
text: How do the routing acceptance tests read the StubRouter dog-leg rule ('left side then right side, nearest first')?
why: Left of travel is the only meaning of 'left' that does not depend on the map projection, and 'nearest first' implies interleaving the two sides at each offset
